items.explain: The sentence compares before and after: letters took days, but phones let people talk right away. ☎️
items.hint: Which sentence tells how talking was different?

items.prompt: Which sentence shows that hummingbirds use a lot of energy?
items.visual: Hummingbirds are some of the smallest birds in the world. Their hearts can beat more than 1,000 times a minute. They visit hundreds of flowers each day to get enough food. They can fly backward. The smallest hummingbirds are only about two inches long.

choices.why: This is a cool fact, but it does not show how much energy they use.

choices.t: They visit hundreds of flowers each day to get enough food.
The smallest hummingbirds are only about two inches long.

items.prompt: The root dict means say. Which word names a book that tells what words mean?
items.say: The root dict means say. Which word names a book that tells what words mean?

choices.why: Transport has the root port, which means carry.
Structure has the root struct, which means build.

items.explain: A dictionary is a book of words. It tells what words mean and how to say them. The root dict means say. 📖
items.hint: Find the word with dict inside it.

items.prompt: These words share the root port. What does port mean?
items.say: These words share the root port. What does port mean?
items.visual: transport   export   portable

choices.why: Pull is the meaning of tract.
Look is the meaning of spect.

items.explain: Port means carry. Trucks transport, or carry, goods. To export is to carry goods out of a country.
items.hint: Think: what does a truck do when it transports things?

items.prompt: Beavers construct dams from sticks and mud. What does construct mean?
items.say: Beavers construct dams from sticks and mud. What does construct mean?

choices.why: Break is the meaning of rupt, not struct.
Look is the meaning of spect, not struct.

items.explain: The root struct means build. Beavers construct, or build, dams. 🦫
items.hint: Which root is inside construct?

items.prompt: rupt means break. What happens when a water pipe ruptures?
items.say: Rupt means break. What happens when a water pipe ruptures?

choices.why: Build is the meaning of struct, not rupt.
Pull is the meaning of tract, not rupt.

items.explain: A pipe that ruptures breaks open, and water leaks out. The root rupt means break.
items.hint: The root rupt means break.

items.prompt: In subtract, sub means away and tract means pull. What does subtract mean?
items.say: In subtract, sub means away and tract means pull. What does subtract mean?

choices.why: Say is the meaning of dict, not tract.
Carry is the meaning of port, not tract.

items.explain: sub (away) + tract (pull) = to pull away. When you subtract 3 from 10, you take 3 away. ➖
items.hint: Put the two meanings together: away + pull.

items.prompt: in means into. spect means look. What does inspect mean?
items.say: In means into. Spect means look. What does inspect mean?

choices.why: Carry is the meaning of port, not spect.
Build is the meaning of struct, not spect.

items.explain: in (into) + spect (look) = to look into. When you inspect a leaf, you look at it closely. 🔍
items.hint: The root spect means look.

items.prompt: uni means one. form means shape. Why does a team wear uniforms?
items.say: Uni means one. Form means shape. Why does a team wear uniforms?

choices.t: so they can carry more things

choices.t: so they can break the rules
choices.why: Break is the meaning of rupt, not form.

items.explain: uni (one) + form (shape) = one shape or look. Team uniforms all look the same. 👕

items.prompt: Which word means "the state of being happy"?

items.prompt: Which word means "the act of agreeing"?

items.hint: Look for the suffix -ment.

items.prompt: Which word means "the act of inventing"?

items.explain: -tion turns an action word into a naming word. Invention = the act of inventing, or the new thing someone invented. 💡
items.hint: Look for the suffix -tion.

items.hint: Try "you are" in the blank.

items.prompt: Tap the sentence that is a simile.

items.hint: Look for the word like or as.

items.prompt: Tap the sentence that is a metaphor.
items.say: Tap the sentence that is a metaphor.

choices.t: The moon rose over the hill.
choices.why: This tells what really happened. It does not compare two things.

items.explain: A metaphor says one thing is another. The moon was not really a coin. The real meaning is that it looked round and shiny. 🌕
items.hint: A metaphor compares without like or as.

items.prompt: "Mia's hands were as cold as ice." What does this really mean?
items.say: Mia's hands were as cold as ice. What does this really mean?

Ice is cold, so this means the opposite of warm.

items.explain: This simile compares Mia's hands to ice. Her hands were not ice. The real meaning is that they were very cold. 🧊

items.prompt: "Noah is a night owl." What does this really mean?
items.say: Noah is a night owl. What does this really mean?

Noah goes to bed very early.

items.explain: This metaphor compares Noah to an owl. Owls are awake at night. The real meaning is that Noah likes to stay up late. 🦉

items.prompt: "The thunder was a drum in the sky." Is this a simile or a metaphor?

items.prompt: "The waves roared like a lion." Is this a simile or a metaphor?

items.hint: Look for like or as.

items.prompt: "The playground was an oven in July." What does this really mean?

items.prompt: "Her smile was as bright as the sun." Which two things are compared?

items.explain: The simile compares her smile to the sun. The real meaning: her smile was big and happy.

items.prompt: "Look outside! It's raining cats and dogs!" What does raining cats and dogs mean?

items.prompt: "The spelling test was a piece of cake." What does this mean?

items.prompt: "Please keep an eye on your little brother." What does this mean?

items.explain: Keep an eye on really means to watch carefully so nothing goes wrong. 👀
items.hint: Why would someone need to watch a little kid?

items.prompt: "Ben was all ears when the ranger talked about bears." What does this mean?
items.say: Ben was all ears when the ranger talked about bears. What does this mean?

choices.why: That is the word-for-word meaning. Ben had two ears, like everyone.

items.explain: All ears really means listening very carefully. Ben was very interested in what the ranger said. 👂
items.hint: What do you use your ears for?

items.prompt: What does the proverb "Two heads are better than one" teach?
items.say: What does the proverb, two heads are better than one, teach?

choices.t: It is better to have two heads.
choices.why: That is the word-for-word meaning. The proverb is about people working together.

choices.t: It is always better to work alone.
choices.why: The proverb says the opposite: sharing ideas helps.

choices.t: Two people working together can solve a problem better than one.

items.hint: What can happen when two people think about the same problem?

items.prompt: What does "Don't judge a book by its cover" mean?
items.say: What does, don't judge a book by its cover, mean?

choices.t: Books with pretty covers are always the best.
choices.why: The proverb says the opposite: looks do not tell you everything.

items.explain: A plain cover can hold a great story. The real lesson: do not decide what someone or something is like just from how it looks. 📚
items.hint: Can you tell if a book is good just by looking at the outside?

items.prompt: "Mia let the cat out of the bag about the surprise party." What does this mean?
items.say: Mia let the cat out of the bag about the surprise party. What does this mean?

choices.t: Mia let a real cat out of a bag.
choices.why: That is the word-for-word meaning. There was no cat and no bag.

choices.t: Mia told the secret before she was supposed to.

choices.why: The idiom means the opposite: the secret got out.

items.explain: Let the cat out of the bag really means to tell a secret, often by accident. Now everyone knows about the surprise party. 🎉
items.hint: What is special about a surprise party?

items.prompt: What does "Actions speak louder than words" mean?
items.say: What does, actions speak louder than words, mean?

choices.why: That is the word-for-word meaning. Actions do not really make sounds.

choices.t: What you do shows more about you than what you say.
Talking is more important than doing.
choices.why: The proverb says the opposite: doing matters more.

items.explain: Actions do not really speak. The real lesson: what you do shows more than what you say. Saying "I will help" means less than really helping.
items.hint: Which shows more: saying you will help, or helping?

items.prompt: Which word fits the sentence?
items.visual: The girl ? kite got stuck in the tree asked for help.

choices.why: "The girl who kite" does not make sense. The kite belongs to the girl.
Which is for things. The sentence needs to show the kite belongs to the girl.

items.explain: Use whose to show belonging. The kite belongs to the girl. 🪁
items.hint: Who does the kite belong to?

items.prompt: Which word fits the sentence?
items.visual: Our class has a turtle, ? sleeps in a glass tank.

choices.why: Who is for people. A turtle is an animal.
When extra information is set off by commas, use which, not that.

items.explain: Use which for things and animals. When the extra information is set off by commas, use which, not that. 🐢
items.hint: Is a turtle a person? Look at the commas.

items.prompt: Which word fits the sentence?
items.visual: The nurse ? helped me was very kind.

choices.why: Which is for things. A nurse is a person.
Whose shows belonging. The sentence tells what the nurse did.

items.explain: Use who for people. The nurse who helped me was very kind.
items.hint: Is a nurse a person or a thing?

items.prompt: Which word fits the sentence?
items.visual: The song ? we learned in music class has five verses.

choices.why: Who is for people. A song is a thing.
Whose shows belonging, like "whose song." It does not fit here.

items.explain: That can be used for things. The song that we learned has five verses. 🎵
items.hint: A song is a thing.

items.prompt: Tap the relative pronoun in this sentence.
items.visual: The boy who found the lost puppy is my cousin.

choices.why: Boy is a noun. It names a person.
Puppy is a noun. It names an animal.

items.explain: Who is the relative pronoun. It starts the part "who found the lost puppy," which tells more about the boy. 🐕
items.hint: Look for who, whose, which, or that.

items.prompt: Which word fits the sentence?
items.visual: An octopus is an animal ? arms have suction cups.

choices.why: "An animal which arms" does not make sense. The arms belong to the octopus.
Who is for people. An octopus is not a person.

items.explain: Use whose to show belonging. The arms belong to the octopus. 🐙
items.hint: Whose arms? The octopus's arms.

items.prompt: Which word fits the sentence?
items.visual: Mount Everest, ? is the highest mountain on Earth, is in Asia.

choices.why: Who is for people. A mountain is a thing.
When extra information is set off by commas, use which, not that.

items.explain: Use which for things. When the extra information is set off by commas, use which. 🏔️
items.hint: Is a mountain a person or a thing? Look at the commas.

items.prompt: Tap the sentence that uses the right relative pronoun.

choices.t: The pilot which flew the plane waved to us.
choices.why: Which is for things. A pilot is a person.

choices.t: The pilot who flew the plane waved to us.
The pilot whose flew the plane waved to us.
choices.why: Whose shows belonging. Nothing belongs to the pilot here.

items.explain: Use who for people. The pilot who flew the plane waved to us. ✈️
items.hint: Is a pilot a person or a thing?

items.prompt: Tap the sentence with commas in the right places.

choices.t: We packed apples cheese, and crackers.
choices.why: A comma is missing between apples and cheese.

choices.t: We packed apples, cheese, and crackers.
We packed, apples, cheese, and crackers.
choices.why: The comma should not go after packed. Commas go between the items in the list.

items.explain: In a list, put a comma after each item before and: apples, cheese, and crackers. 🍎
items.hint: Put a comma between each thing in the list.

items.prompt: Tap the sentence with the comma in the right place.

choices.t: The wind blew, and the leaves fell.
The wind blew and, the leaves fell.
choices.why: The comma goes before and, not after it.

choices.t: The wind, blew and the leaves fell.
choices.why: The comma should not split "The wind blew."

items.explain: "The wind blew" and "the leaves fell" are two sentences joined by and. Put the comma before and. 🍂
items.hint: Find the joining word. The comma goes just before it.

items.prompt: Tap the sentence with the comma in the right place.

choices.t: No I have, not seen your hat.
choices.why: The comma should not split "have not seen."

choices.t: No I, have not seen your hat.
choices.why: The comma goes right after the starting word No.

choices.t: No, I have not seen your hat.

items.explain: Put a comma after a starting word like yes, no, or well.
items.hint: Where would you pause after the first word?

items.prompt: Tap the sentence with the comma in the right place.

choices.t: First mix, the flour and water.
choices.why: The comma goes right after the starting word First.

choices.t: First, mix the flour and water.
First mix the, flour and water.
choices.why: This comma splits "the flour" in the wrong place.

items.explain: First is a starting word. Put a comma right after it.
items.hint: Pause after the first word.

items.prompt: Tap the sentence with the comma in the right place.

choices.t: We can play outside, or we can read inside.
We can play outside or, we can read inside.
choices.why: The comma goes before or, not after it.

items.explain: "We can play outside" and "we can read inside" are two sentences joined by or. The comma goes before or.
items.hint: The comma goes before the joining word.

items.prompt: Why does this sentence need commas?
items.visual: Frogs, toads, and newts live near the pond.

choices.t: They separate items in a list.

choices.why: There is only one sentence here. There is no joining word like but or so between two sentences.

choices.t: They come after a starting word.
choices.why: Frogs is not a starting word like yes or well. It is the first item in a list.

items.explain: Frogs, toads, and newts is a list of three animals. Commas go between the items. 🐸
items.hint: Count the animals in the sentence.

items.prompt: Why does this sentence need a comma?
items.visual: The sky was dark, so we went inside.

choices.t: It separates items in a list.
choices.why: There is no list in this sentence.

choices.t: It comes after a starting word.
choices.why: The first word is The. It is not a starting word like yes or well.

items.explain: "The sky was dark" and "we went inside" are two sentences. The comma goes before so, which joins them.
items.hint: Look for a joining word like and, but, or so.

items.prompt: Tap the sentence with commas in the right places.

choices.t: We saw lions zebras and, giraffes at the zoo.
choices.why: A comma is missing after lions, and the comma after and is in the wrong place.

choices.t: We saw lions, zebras, and, giraffes at the zoo.
choices.why: There should not be a comma after and.

choices.t: We saw lions, zebras, and giraffes at the zoo.

items.explain: This is a list of animals: lions, zebras, and giraffes. No comma goes after and. 🦓
items.hint: Commas go between the animals in the list.

items.prompt: Which word best joins the two parts?
items.visual: The puppy was tired, ? it took a nap.

choices.why: But shows a difference. Napping when you are tired is not a difference.
Or shows a choice. There is no choice here.

items.explain: so shows a result. The puppy was tired, so it took a nap. 🐶
items.hint: The nap is the result of being tired.

items.prompt: Which word best joins the two parts?
items.visual: Maya studied the map, ? she still got lost.

choices.why: So shows a result. Studying a map does not make you get lost.
For means because. Studying the map is not the reason she got lost.

items.explain: yet shows a difference, like but. Maya studied the map, yet she still got lost. That is a surprise. 🗺️
items.hint: Is getting lost after studying a map expected, or a surprise?

items.prompt: Which word best joins the two parts?
items.visual: We can walk to the library, ? we can ride our bikes.

choices.why: So shows a result. This sentence gives two choices.
Nor adds another "not." Neither part says not.

items.explain: or shows a choice: walk or ride our bikes. 🚲
items.hint: The sentence gives two choices.

items.prompt: Which word best joins the two parts?
items.visual: Sam brought an umbrella, ? the forecast said rain.

choices.why: Or shows a choice. Sam did not have to choose between these.
Nor adds another "not." Neither part says not.

items.explain: Here for means because. Sam brought an umbrella because the forecast said rain. ☔
items.hint: Why did Sam bring an umbrella?

items.prompt: Which word is not a FANBOYS conjunction?
items.say: Which word is not a fan boys conjunction?

choices.why: Nor is the N in FANBOYS.
So is the S in FANBOYS.

items.explain: FANBOYS: for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so. Although is a joining word, but it is not one of the FANBOYS.
items.hint: Say the letters: F, A, N, B, O, Y, S.

items.prompt: Which sentence best joins "The wind was strong" and "The kite flew high"?
items.say: Which sentence best joins, the wind was strong, and, the kite flew high?

choices.t: The wind was strong, so the kite flew high.
The wind was strong so, the kite flew high.
choices.why: The comma goes before so, not after it.

choices.t: The wind was strong, or the kite flew high.
choices.why: Or shows a choice. Both things happened.

items.explain: The kite flew high as a result of the strong wind, so use , so. The comma goes before so. 🪁
items.hint: Which part happened because of the other? Check the comma too.

items.prompt: In this sentence, what does yet mean?
items.say: In this sentence, what does yet mean?
items.visual: The trail was long, yet the kids kept hiking.

choices.why: So shows a result. A long trail is not a reason to keep hiking.
Or shows a choice. There is no choice here.

items.explain: Here yet means but. The trail was long, but the kids did not stop. 🥾
items.hint: Do the two parts go together, or is the second part a surprise?

items.prompt: Which word best joins the two parts?
items.visual: The cheetah is very fast, ? it cannot run far without resting.

choices.why: So shows a result. Being fast is not the reason a cheetah needs rest.
Or shows a choice. Both parts are true.

items.explain: but shows a difference. The cheetah is fast, but it gets tired quickly. Cheetahs can only sprint for a short distance. 🐆
items.hint: Do the two parts go together, or do they clash?

items.prompt: What is the theme of this fable?
items.visual: The Wind and the Sun argued about who was stronger. They saw a man walking in a coat. "Whoever gets his coat off wins," said the Sun. The Wind blew hard, but the man held his coat tighter. Then the Sun shone warm and gentle. Soon the man felt hot and took off his coat.

choices.t: The Sun is hotter than the Wind.
choices.why: That is a detail from the story, not the lesson.

choices.t: Being gentle can work better than being rough.
Always wear a coat on windy days.
choices.why: The coat is a detail. The story is about how the Sun won.

items.explain: Clue: the Wind "blew hard," but the man "held his coat tighter." The Sun was warm and gentle, and it won.
items.hint: Which way worked: blowing hard or shining gently?

items.prompt: What is the theme of this story?
items.visual: Lena and Jay both entered the science fair. That morning, Jay's plant display fell and broke. Lena had planned to practice her speech, but she helped Jay fix his display instead. Jay's project won a ribbon. Lena did not win, but she smiled. "Helping you felt better than any ribbon," she said.

choices.t: You should always try to win first.
choices.why: Lena did not win, but she was happy she helped.
That is a detail. The story is about Lena choosing to help.

choices.t: Helping a friend can matter more than winning.

items.explain: Clue: "Helping you felt better than any ribbon," she said. Lena chose to help her friend. 🎗️
items.hint: Read what Lena says at the end.

items.prompt: What is the theme of this fable?
items.visual: A dog was carrying a bone across a bridge. It looked down into the river and saw its own reflection. The dog thought it was another dog with a bigger bone. It wanted that bone too, so it barked. When it opened its mouth, its own bone fell into the water and sank.

choices.t: Wanting too much can make you lose what you have.

choices.why: That is a fact about dogs, not the lesson.

choices.t: Rivers are good places to swim.
choices.why: The river is a detail. The dog did not swim.

items.explain: Clue: the dog wanted the other bone too, so it opened its mouth, and its own bone fell in the river. Being greedy made it lose what it had. 🦴
items.hint: Why did the dog end up with no bone?

items.prompt: What is the theme of this story?
items.visual: Ivy never wanted to try new foods. At her aunt's house, there was a bowl of orange fruit called mango. Ivy almost said no. Then she took one small bite. It was sweet and juicy! "I'm glad I tried it," Ivy said. Now mango is her favorite fruit.

choices.why: That is a detail from the story, not the lesson.

choices.t: Be brave and try new things.
Only eat foods you already know.
choices.why: Ivy tried something new and loved it. The story says the opposite.

items.explain: Clue: "I'm glad I tried it," Ivy said. She was nervous, but trying something new turned out great. 🥭
items.hint: What did Ivy learn after her first bite?

items.prompt: Which sentence from the story best shows the theme?
items.visual: Max built a birdhouse, but the roof fell off. He was upset. Then he looked closely and saw that he had used too few nails. He built it again with more nails. "Mistakes can teach you how to do better," his grandpa said. This time, a wren moved in.

choices.t: Max built a birdhouse, but the roof fell off.
choices.why: This is the problem in the story, not the lesson.

choices.t: "Mistakes can teach you how to do better," his grandpa said.
This time, a wren moved in.
choices.why: This is how the story ends, but it does not state the lesson.

items.explain: The theme is that you can learn from mistakes. Grandpa's words, "Mistakes can teach you how to do better," say it directly. 🐦
items.hint: Which sentence tells a lesson Max could use again?

items.prompt: What is the theme of this fable?
items.visual: A tall oak tree laughed at the thin reeds by the river. "You bend with every breeze," it said. "I stand strong." One night, a big storm came. The oak would not bend, and some of its branches snapped. The reeds bent low in the wind. In the morning, they stood up straight again.

choices.t: Oak trees are taller than reeds.
choices.why: That is a fact from the story, not the lesson.
The storm is a detail. The story is about bending.

choices.t: Being willing to bend and change can help you get through hard times.

items.explain: Clue: the oak "would not bend," and its branches broke. The reeds "bent low" and stood up again. Bending helped them.
items.hint: Which plant was fine in the morning, and why?

items.prompt: What is the theme of this story?
items.visual: Sofia planted bean seeds in a cup. The next day, she dug them up to check if they were growing. She did this every day, and nothing grew. Her teacher helped her plant new seeds. "This time, just water them and wait," he said. Sofia waited. After one week, green sprouts poked out of the soil.

choices.t: Some things take time, so be patient.
Seeds should be dug up every day.
choices.why: Digging up the seeds is why they did not grow the first time.
The beans grew fine when Sofia waited.

items.explain: Clue: the first time, Sofia dug them up "to check," and they did not grow. The second time, she waited, and they sprouted. 🌱
items.hint: What did Sofia do differently the second time?

items.prompt: What is the theme of this story?
items.visual: Theo was new at school. At recess, he stood alone by the fence. Ana walked over and asked him to join her group. Theo taught them a new game from his old school. Soon, even more kids wanted to play. Everyone had fun, and Theo smiled all afternoon.

choices.t: Recess is the best part of the day.
choices.why: The story does not say this. It is about including Theo.

choices.t: Including others can make things better for everyone.

choices.why: When Ana invited Theo, everyone had more fun. The story says the opposite.

items.explain: Clue: Ana invited Theo, he taught a new game, and "everyone had fun." Including him made recess better for all. ⚽
items.hint: What happened after Ana invited Theo?

items.prompt: Which text is a first-hand account?
items.visual:
Text 1 Last summer, my brother and I explored tide pools at the beach. I found a purple sea star stuck to a rock. I looked closely and saw tiny bumps all over its arms. We also spotted little crabs hiding under seaweed. I could have stayed there all day!
Text 2 Sea stars live in oceans all over the world. Many live in tide pools, where water is left behind when the tide goes out. Most sea stars have five arms. If a sea star loses an arm, it can grow a new one. Sea stars are not fish, so scientists like to call them sea stars instead of starfish.

choices.why: Text 2 gives facts. The writer does not say they were there.
Only Text 1 uses I and tells what the writer saw and felt.

items.explain: Text 1 says "I found a purple sea star." The writer was there, so it is a first-hand account.
items.hint: Which text uses the word I?

items.prompt: What does Text 2 tell that Text 1 does not?
items.say: What does Text 2 tell that Text 1 does not?

choices.why: Both texts tell about sea stars in tide pools.

items.prompt: Which text is a second-hand account?
items.visual:
Text 1 My family waited on a bench near Old Faithful in Yellowstone National Park. At first, only a little steam rose from the ground. Then, with a loud whoosh, hot water shot high into the sky! Warm mist drifted over the crowd. My little sister clapped and cheered.
Text 2 Old Faithful is a geyser in Yellowstone National Park. A geyser is a hot spring that shoots water and steam into the air. Deep underground, hot rocks heat the water until it bursts out. Old Faithful erupts about every hour and a half. Its water can shoot more than 100 feet high.

choices.why: Text 1 is first-hand. The writer says "My family waited on a bench."

items.explain: Text 2 gives facts without saying the writer was there. That makes it a second-hand account.
items.hint: Which text does not use I, my, or we?

items.prompt: What does Text 2 explain that Text 1 does not?
items.say: What does Text 2 explain that Text 1 does not?
items.visual:

choices.t: that hot water shoots into the air
choices.why: Both texts tell about water shooting into the air.

choices.t: what makes the water burst out

choices.why: Only Text 1 tells about the sister.

items.hint: Which text explains how a geyser works?

items.say: Text 1 says the water shot high into the sky. Which detail from Text 2 tells how high?

items.prompt: geo means earth. -ology means study of. What is geology?
items.say: Geo means earth. The ending ology means study of. What is geology?

choices.why: That is biology. Bio means life.

choices.t: the study of Earth's rocks and land

choices.why: Stars are far out in space. Geo means earth.

items.explain: geo (earth) + -ology (study of) = the study of Earth, like its rocks and land. 🪨
items.hint: Put the two meanings together.

items.prompt: micro means small. phone means sound. What does a microphone do?
items.say: Micro means small. Phone means sound. What does a microphone do?

choices.why: Heat is the meaning of therm.

choices.t: It helps you see far away.
choices.why: Far is the meaning of tele.

choices.t: It picks up small sounds so they can be made louder.

items.explain: micro (small) + phone (sound). A microphone picks up even small sounds, like a soft voice, so a speaker can make them louder. 🎤
items.hint: Put the two meanings together: small + sound.

items.prompt: auto means self. graph means write. What is an autograph?
items.say: Auto means self. Graph means write. What is an autograph?

choices.t: a person's name, written by that person

choices.why: That is a photograph. Photo means light.
Geo means earth. There is no geo in autograph.

items.explain: auto (self) + graph (write) = writing by yourself. When an author signs your book, you get an autograph. ✍️
items.hint: auto = self. graph = write.

items.prompt: Which word has a root that means heat?
items.say: Which word has a root that means heat?

choices.why: Hydrant has the root hydro, which means water.
Microbe has the root micro, which means small.

items.explain: therm means heat. Thermal socks keep your feet warm. 🧦
items.hint: Which word has therm inside it?

items.prompt: Which word has a root that means light?
items.say: Which word has a root that means light?

choices.why: Thermometer has the root therm, which means heat.
Geography has the root geo, which means earth.

items.explain: photo means light. In photosynthesis, plants use sunlight to make food. 🌱
items.hint: Which word starts with photo?

items.prompt: micro means small. bio means life. What is a microbe?
items.say: Micro means small. Bio means life. What is a microbe?

choices.why: Micro means small, so a microbe is tiny, not huge.
Hydro means water. Microbe has micro and bio.

items.explain: micro (small) + bio (life) = a tiny living thing. Most microbes are so small you need a microscope to see them. 🦠
items.hint: Put the two meanings together: small + life.

items.prompt: A seismograph is a machine used to study earthquakes. The root graph tells you the machine does what?
items.say: A seismograph is a machine used to study earthquakes. The root graph tells you the machine does what?

choices.why: Heat is the meaning of therm.

choices.t: It writes or draws a record.

choices.why: Light is the meaning of photo.

items.explain: graph means write. A seismograph draws wiggly lines that show how much the ground shook.
items.hint: What does graph mean?

items.prompt: tele means far. graph means write. What was a telegraph?
items.say: Tele means far. Graph means write. What was a telegraph?

choices.t: a tool for seeing tiny things
choices.why: Tiny is the meaning of micro. Telegraph has tele and graph.
That is a biography. Bio means life.

choices.t: a machine that sent written messages far away

items.explain: tele (far) + graph (write) = writing sent far away. Before phones, people used the telegraph to send messages over wires.
items.hint: tele = far. graph = write.

items.prompt: What does nocturnal mean in this sentence?
items.say: What does nocturnal mean in this sentence?
items.visual: Owls are nocturnal, which means they are awake at night and sleep during the day.

choices.why: The sentence is about when owls are awake, not where they live.
The sentence does not talk about food.

items.explain: Clue: "which means they are awake at night and sleep during the day." 🦉
items.hint: Read the words after "which means."

items.prompt: What does migrate mean in this sentence?
items.say: What does migrate mean in this sentence?
items.visual: Each fall, many geese migrate, flying south to find warmer weather and food.

choices.why: The geese are flying south, not building.

choices.t: to travel far to a new place when the season changes

choices.why: That is hibernate. The geese are flying, not sleeping.

items.explain: Clue: "flying south to find warmer weather." The geese move to a new place each fall.
items.hint: Read the words right after the comma.

items.prompt: What does camouflage mean in this sentence?
items.say: What does camouflage mean in this sentence?
items.visual: The snowshoe hare's white winter fur is camouflage. It blends in with the snow, so the hare is hard to see.

choices.t: a warm nest under the snow
choices.why: The sentence is about the hare's fur, not a nest.
The sentence does not talk about food.

choices.t: colors that help an animal blend in and hide

items.explain: Clue: "It blends in with the snow, so the hare is hard to see." 🐇
items.hint: What does the white fur do?

items.prompt: What does fragile mean in this sentence?
items.say: What does fragile mean in this sentence?
items.visual: Be careful with the robin eggs because they are fragile and can crack easily.

choices.why: The clue is about cracking, not weight.
The clue is about cracking, not temperature.

items.explain: Clue: "they can crack easily." Something fragile breaks easily. 🥚
items.hint: What can happen to the eggs?

items.prompt: What does abundant mean in this sentence?
items.say: What does abundant mean in this sentence?
items.visual: Acorns are abundant in the fall. The ground under the oak tree is covered with hundreds of them.

choices.why: Hundreds of acorns is a lot, not a few.
The sentence tells how many acorns there are, not if they are bad.

items.explain: Clue: "The ground ... is covered with hundreds of them." That is a lot of acorns. 🌰
items.hint: Are there a few acorns or a lot?

items.prompt: What does dormant mean in this sentence?
items.say: What does dormant mean in this sentence?
items.visual: The volcano is dormant. It has not erupted in hundreds of years, but it could erupt again someday.

choices.why: It has not erupted in hundreds of years.
The sentence says it could erupt again someday.

items.explain: Clue: "It has not erupted in hundreds of years, but it could erupt again." Dormant means quiet for now. 🌋
items.hint: Is the volcano active now? Could it be active later?

items.prompt: What does predator mean in this sentence?
items.say: What does predator mean in this sentence?
items.visual: A hawk is a predator. It hunts and eats smaller animals, such as mice.

choices.t: an animal that hunts other animals for food
an animal that eats only plants
choices.why: The hawk eats mice, which are animals.
Hawks can fly. The clue is about hunting.

items.explain: Clue: "It hunts and eats smaller animals." That is what a predator does. 🦅
items.hint: Read the sentence right after the word.

items.prompt: What does transparent mean in this sentence?
items.say: What does transparent mean in this sentence?
items.visual: The jellyfish is almost transparent, so you can see right through its body.

choices.why: If it were brightly colored, you could not see through it.

choices.t: clear, so you can see through it

choices.why: Jellyfish are soft. The clue is about seeing through.

items.explain: Clue: "you can see right through its body." Transparent means see-through, like clear glass.
items.hint: What can you do when you look at the jellyfish?

items.prompt: Tap the sentence that uses personification.
items.say: Tap the sentence that uses personification.

choices.t: The alarm clock rang at seven.
choices.why: Alarm clocks really ring. This is not a human action.

choices.t: The alarm clock yelled at me to wake up.
My alarm clock is a million times louder than thunder.
choices.why: This is a huge exaggeration. That is hyperbole.

items.explain: Only people can yell. "The alarm clock yelled" gives the clock a human action. Real meaning: the alarm was very loud. ⏰
items.hint: Which sentence makes the clock act like a person?

items.prompt: Tap the sentence that uses hyperbole.
items.say: Tap the sentence that uses hyperbole.

choices.t: This homework will take me a hundred years!
This homework will take me an hour.
choices.why: An hour could really be true. It is not an exaggeration.

choices.t: The homework stared at me from the table.
choices.why: Homework staring is personification, not hyperbole.

items.explain: No homework takes a hundred years. It is a huge exaggeration. Real meaning: the homework will take a long time.
items.hint: Which sentence stretches the truth way too far?

items.prompt: "The thunder grumbled in the distance." Which kind of language is this?
items.say: The thunder grumbled in the distance. Which kind of language is this?

choices.why: Hyperbole is a big exaggeration. This gives thunder a human action.

items.explain: Only people grumble. Thunder cannot really grumble, so this is personification. Real meaning: the thunder made a low, rumbling sound far away. ⛈️
items.hint: Can thunder really grumble like a person?

items.prompt: "I've told you a thousand times to shut the door!" What does this really mean?
items.say: I've told you a thousand times to shut the door! What does this really mean?

choices.t: The speaker said it exactly 1,000 times.
choices.why: That is the word-for-word meaning. The speaker did not really say it 1,000 times.

choices.t: The speaker has said it many times.
The speaker has never said it before.
choices.why: The saying means the opposite: many times.

items.explain: This is hyperbole. The speaker did not really say it a thousand times. The real meaning: they have said it many times and want you to remember.
items.hint: Is the speaker giving an exact number, or stretching the truth?

items.prompt: "The old house groaned in the storm." What does this really mean?
items.say: The old house groaned in the storm. What does this really mean?

choices.t: The house felt sad and hurt.
choices.why: That is the word-for-word meaning. Houses cannot feel.
The sentence does not say the house fell.

choices.t: The house made creaking noises in the wind.

items.explain: This is personification. A house cannot groan like a person. The real meaning: the wind made the house creak and make noises. 🌬️
items.hint: What sounds can an old house make in strong wind?

items.prompt: "Kai's smile was a mile wide." Which kind of language is this?
items.say: Kai's smile was a mile wide. Which kind of language is this?

choices.why: Personification gives a thing human actions. Kai is a person, and people really smile.

items.explain: No smile is really a mile wide. That is an exaggeration, so it is hyperbole. Real meaning: Kai had a very big smile. 😁
items.hint: Can a smile really be a mile wide?

items.prompt: "The stars winked at us from the night sky." What does this really mean?
items.say: The stars winked at us from the night sky. What does this really mean?

choices.t: The stars twinkled, looking bright and then dim.

choices.why: That is the word-for-word meaning. Stars do not have eyes.

choices.t: The stars fell out of the sky.
choices.why: The sentence does not say the stars fell.

items.explain: This is personification. Stars cannot wink. The real meaning: the stars seemed to twinkle, flashing bright and dim. ✨
items.hint: What do stars look like on a clear night?

items.prompt: "I'm so tired I could sleep for a year." What does this really mean?
items.say: I'm so tired I could sleep for a year. What does this really mean?

choices.t: The speaker plans to sleep for 365 days.
choices.why: That is the word-for-word meaning. No person sleeps for a year.

choices.t: The speaker is not sleepy at all.
choices.why: The saying means the opposite: very sleepy.

items.explain: This is hyperbole. Nobody could sleep for a whole year. The real meaning: the speaker is very tired. 😴
items.hint: Why would someone say something so big?

items.prompt: Tap the sentence that keeps the same verb tense.

choices.t: The frog hopped onto the log and croaks.
choices.why: Hopped is past, but croaks is present.

choices.t: The frog hops onto the log and croaks.
The frog hops onto the log and croaked.
choices.why: Hops is present, but croaked is past.

items.explain: Hops and croaks are both present tense. 🐸
items.hint: Both verbs should be in the same time.

items.prompt: Which verb fits the sentence?
items.visual: Last night, the owl ? on a branch and hooted.

choices.why: Sits is present. Last night and hooted show the past.
Will sit is future. Last night and hooted show the past.

items.explain: Last night and hooted show the past, so use sat. 🦉
items.hint: Look at the words Last night.

items.prompt: Which verb fits the sentence?
items.visual: Every spring, the robins ? back and build nests.

choices.why: Came is past. Build is present, and this happens every spring.
Will come is future. Build is present, and this happens every spring.

items.explain: Build is present tense, so use come. Things that happen every year use present tense. 🐦
items.hint: Match the tense of build.

items.prompt: Which verb fits the sentence?
items.visual: Next week, Grandpa will arrive and ? us to the zoo.

choices.why: Took is past. Next week and will arrive show the future.
Taken needs a helper like have. Next week shows the future.

items.explain: "Grandpa will arrive and (will) take us." Both verbs are in the future. 🦁
items.hint: The word will goes with both verbs.

items.prompt: Which verb does not match the others?
items.say: Which verb does not match the others?
items.visual: Leo washes the dishes, dries them, and stacked them.

choices.why: Washes is present, like dries. It matches.
Dries is present, like washes. It matches.

items.explain: Washes and dries are present. Stacked is past. It should be stacks. 🍽️
items.hint: Two verbs are present. Which one is not?

items.prompt: Which sentence fixes the tense mistake?
items.visual: Mia painted a picture and shows it to her class.

choices.t: Mia painted a picture and showing it to her class.
choices.why: Showing needs a helper like was. It is not a complete verb here.

choices.t: Mia painted a picture and showed it to her class.
Mia paints a picture and showed it to her class.
choices.why: Paints is present, but showed is past. The tenses still do not match.

items.explain: Painted and showed are both past tense. 🎨
items.hint: Make the second verb match painted.

items.prompt: Which verb fits the sentence?
items.visual: Yesterday, the scientists ? the volcano and took rock samples.

choices.why: Study is present. Yesterday and took show the past.
Will study is future. Yesterday and took show the past.

items.explain: Yesterday and took show the past, so use studied. 🌋
items.hint: Look at the word Yesterday.

items.prompt: Tap the sentence that switches tense by mistake.

choices.t: The bees buzz and gather pollen.
choices.why: Buzz and gather are both present. The tense matches.

choices.t: The bees buzzed and gather pollen.
The bees buzzed and gathered pollen.
choices.why: Buzzed and gathered are both past. The tense matches.

items.explain: Buzzed is past, but gather is present. That is a tense switch. 🐝
items.hint: Check if both verbs are in the same time.

items.prompt: Which words complete the pair?
items.visual: Whales are not only huge ? smart.

choices.why: The partner of not only is but also.
Or goes with either, not with not only.

items.explain: Not only goes with but also. Whales are not only huge but also smart. 🐋
items.hint: Not only ____ ____.

items.prompt: Which word completes the pair?
items.visual: Either we leave now, ? we will miss the bus.

choices.why: Nor goes with neither, not either.
And goes with both, not either.

items.explain: Either goes with or. Either we leave now, or we will miss the bus. 🚌
items.hint: Either and ____ are partners.

items.prompt: Which word completes the pair?
items.visual: Neither the frog ? the toad has fur.

choices.why: Or goes with either. Neither goes with nor.
And goes with both. Neither goes with nor.

items.explain: Neither goes with nor. Neither the frog nor the toad has fur. 🐸
items.hint: Neither and ____ both start with n.

items.prompt: Which word completes the pair?
items.visual: Both lions ? tigers are big cats.

choices.why: Nor goes with neither. Both goes with and.
Or goes with either. Both goes with and.

items.explain: Both goes with and. Both lions and tigers are big cats. 🐯
items.hint: Both and ____ are partners.

items.prompt: Tap the sentence that uses the pair correctly.

choices.t: Neither Ava or Omar was late.
choices.why: Neither goes with nor, not or.

choices.t: Neither Ava nor Omar was late.
Either Ava nor Omar was late.
choices.why: Either goes with or, not nor.

items.explain: Neither goes with nor. Neither Ava nor Omar was late. ⏰
items.hint: Check that each pair has the right partner.

items.prompt: Which pair of words goes together correctly?

choices.why: Not only goes with but also, not nor.
Either goes with or, not and.

items.explain: The correct pairs: either ... or, neither ... nor, both ... and, not only ... but also.
items.hint: Which partner does not only need?

items.prompt: This sentence has a mistake. Which word should replace or?
items.say: This sentence has a mistake. Which word should replace or?
items.visual: Both the snake or the lizard are reptiles.

choices.why: Nor goes with neither. This sentence starts with both.
But is not a partner for both.

items.explain: Both goes with and. Both the snake and the lizard are reptiles. 🦎
items.hint: Find the first word of the pair. What is its partner?

items.prompt: Tap the sentence that uses the pair correctly.

choices.t: The owl is not only quiet and also quick.
choices.why: The partner of not only is but also, not and also.

choices.t: The owl is both quiet nor quick.
choices.why: Both goes with and, not nor.

choices.t: The owl is not only quiet but also quick.

items.explain: Not only goes with but also. The owl is not only quiet but also quick. 🦉
items.hint: Check that each pair has the right partner.

items.prompt: Which word best fits the sentence?
items.visual: The ice cream melted ? it sat in the hot sun.

choices.why: Unless means only if not. It does not fit here.
Although shows a surprise. Ice cream melting in the sun is not a surprise.

items.explain: because gives the reason. The ice cream melted because it sat in the hot sun. 🍦
items.hint: The hot sun is the reason.

items.prompt: Which word best fits the sentence?
items.visual: ? the trail was steep, we hiked all the way to the top.

choices.why: A steep trail is not a reason to keep going. It makes hiking harder.
Unless means only if not. It does not fit here.

items.explain: Although shows a surprise or contrast. The trail was hard, but we still made it to the top. ⛰️
items.hint: Is reaching the top of a steep trail easy, or a surprise?

items.prompt: Which word best fits the sentence?
items.visual: ? the moon is full, the night sky is brighter.

choices.why: Although shows a surprise. A brighter sky during a full moon is not a surprise.
Unless means if not. The sky is brighter when the moon is full, not when it is not full.

items.explain: When tells the time. When the moon is full, the night sky is brighter. 🌕
items.hint: The sentence tells what happens at a certain time.

items.prompt: Tap the subordinating conjunction in this sentence.
items.visual: Although the puppy was small, it barked loudly.

choices.why: Puppy is a noun. It names an animal.
Loudly tells how the puppy barked.

items.explain: Although starts the part that shows a contrast: "although the puppy was small." 🐶
items.hint: Look for a word like because, since, when, or although.

items.prompt: Tap the complex sentence.

choices.t: Because the river flooded, the road was closed.
The river flooded, so the road was closed.
choices.why: This joins two sentences with so. That makes a compound sentence.
This is one simple sentence.

items.explain: "Because the river flooded" cannot stand alone. It is joined to a full sentence, so it is a complex sentence.
items.hint: Look for when, because, since, although, or unless.

items.prompt: Tap the sentence with the comma in the right place.

choices.t: When the leaves change, color fall has arrived.
choices.why: The comma splits "change color." It goes after color.

choices.t: When, the leaves change color fall has arrived.
choices.why: The comma should not come right after when.

choices.t: When the leaves change color, fall has arrived.

items.explain: When a sentence starts with when, put a comma at the end of that first part: "When the leaves change color," 🍁
items.hint: Find where the "when" part ends.

items.prompt: Which word best fits the sentence?
items.visual: The pond froze ? the temperature dropped below freezing.

choices.why: Although shows a surprise. Water freezing in cold weather is not a surprise.
Unless means if not. It does not fit here.

items.explain: Here since means because. The pond froze since the temperature dropped below freezing. ❄️
items.hint: The cold temperature is the reason.

items.prompt: Which sentence best joins "The baby was sleeping" and "We whispered"?
items.say: Which sentence best joins, the baby was sleeping, and, we whispered?

choices.t: Although the baby was sleeping, we whispered.
choices.why: Although shows a surprise. Whispering near a sleeping baby is not a surprise.

choices.t: Because the baby was sleeping, we whispered.
Unless the baby was sleeping, we whispered.
choices.why: Unless means if not. This would mean we whispered only if the baby was not sleeping, which does not make sense.

items.explain: The sleeping baby is the reason we whispered, so use because. 👶
items.hint: Which part is the reason for the other?

items.prompt: Tap the best summary of the passage.
items.visual: Beavers are skilled builders. They cut down small trees with their strong front teeth. They pile branches, rocks, and mud across a stream to make a dam. The dam blocks the water and makes a pond. In the pond, beavers build a home called a lodge, where they stay safe and dry.

choices.why: This is only one small detail.
This is an opinion. The passage does not say it.

choices.t: Beavers use trees, rocks, and mud to build dams that make ponds, where they build safe homes.

items.explain: The passage tells how beavers build dams, make ponds, and build homes. The best summary covers all of it. 🦫
items.hint: Which choice covers the whole passage?

items.prompt: Tap the best summary of the passage.
items.visual: Emperor penguins raise their chicks in Antarctica, the coldest place on Earth. The mother lays one egg and then goes to the sea to eat. The father holds the egg on his feet, under a warm flap of skin. He keeps it warm for about two months. When the chick hatches, the mother comes back with food.

choices.t: Emperor penguin parents work together: the father keeps the egg warm, and the mother brings food.

choices.why: This is too small. It leaves out the main idea.

choices.t: Emperor penguins live in hot jungles.
choices.why: The passage says they live in the coldest place on Earth.

items.explain: The passage tells what the father does and what the mother does. The best summary includes both. 🐧
items.hint: What do the mother and father each do?

items.prompt: Tap the best summary of the passage.
items.visual: The Moon does not make its own light. It reflects light from the Sun. As the Moon travels around Earth, we see different amounts of its sunny side. That is why the Moon seems to change shape. These shapes are called phases, and they repeat about once a month.

choices.why: This is one detail. It does not explain the phases.

choices.t: The Moon reflects sunlight, and as it circles Earth, we see different amounts of its lit side, which makes its phases.
The Moon changes shape because it breaks into pieces.
choices.why: The passage says the Moon only seems to change shape.

items.explain: The passage explains why the Moon seems to change shape. The best summary includes sunlight, the Moon's trip around Earth, and phases. 🌓
items.hint: Which choice explains the whole idea?

items.prompt: Tap the best summary of the passage.
items.visual: Earthworms help gardens grow. As they tunnel through the ground, they make spaces for air and water. They eat dead leaves and turn them into rich soil. Plant roots can grow more easily in soil with worms. That is why gardeners are happy to find worms.

choices.why: This is only one detail.

choices.t: Gardeners should get rid of worms.
choices.why: The passage says gardeners are happy to find worms.

choices.t: Earthworms help plants grow by loosening the soil and turning dead leaves into rich soil.

items.explain: Every sentence tells how worms help plants grow. The best summary says how. 🪱
items.hint: What is almost every sentence about?

items.prompt: Tap the best summary of the passage.
items.visual: Tardigrades are tiny animals, only about half a millimeter long. They are sometimes called water bears. They live in moss, in the deep sea, and even on mountains. When their home dries out, they curl up and can survive like that for years. When water returns, they become active again.

choices.t: Tiny tardigrades can live in many places and can survive being dried out for years.
Tardigrades are sometimes called water bears.
choices.why: This is only one detail.

choices.t: Tardigrades are big bears that live in lakes.
choices.why: The passage says they are tiny, about half a millimeter long.

items.explain: The passage tells where tardigrades live and how they survive drying out. The best summary covers both. 🔬
items.hint: Where do they live, and what can they survive?

items.prompt: Tap the best summary of the passage.
items.visual: Lightning is a giant spark of electricity in the sky. It forms inside storm clouds when tiny bits of ice bump together. Lightning heats the air around it very quickly. The hot air spreads out so fast that it makes a loud boom. That boom is thunder.

choices.why: This is too small. It leaves out lightning and how thunder is made.

choices.t: Lightning is a giant spark from storm clouds, and its heat makes the boom we call thunder.
Lightning is made by the Sun.
choices.why: The passage says lightning forms inside storm clouds.

items.explain: The passage tells what lightning is and how it makes thunder. The best summary covers both. ⚡
items.hint: What is lightning, and how does it make thunder?

items.prompt: Tap the best summary of the passage.
items.visual: Plants cannot walk, but their seeds can travel. Dandelion seeds float on the wind. Burrs stick to animal fur. Coconuts can float across the ocean. Birds eat berries and drop the seeds far away. Moving helps seeds find new places to grow.

choices.t: Dandelion seeds float on the wind.
choices.why: This is only one example.

choices.t: Plants can walk to new places.
choices.why: The passage says plants cannot walk.

choices.t: Seeds travel in many ways, like by wind, water, and animals, to find new places to grow.

items.explain: The passage gives many ways seeds travel and tells why. The best summary covers both. 🌼
items.hint: Which choice covers all the ways, not just one?

items.prompt: Tap the best summary of the passage.
items.visual: A glacier is a huge sheet of ice that moves very slowly. It forms where more snow falls each winter than melts each summer. Over many years, the snow gets packed down into ice. As a glacier slides, it scrapes rocks and carves out valleys. Some glaciers are hundreds of feet thick.

choices.t: Glaciers form from snow packed into ice over many years, and they slowly move and shape the land.
Some glaciers are hundreds of feet thick.
choices.why: This is only one detail.

choices.t: Glaciers melt away in one day.
choices.why: The passage says glaciers form over many years.

items.explain: The passage tells how glaciers form and how they move and shape the land. The best summary covers both. 🏔️
items.hint: How do glaciers form, and what do they do?

items.prompt: Tap the sentence that is an opinion.
items.say: Tap the sentence that is an opinion.

choices.t: In the United States, summer starts in June.
choices.why: This is a fact. You can check it on a calendar.

choices.t: Summer is the best season of the year.
Many plants grow quickly in summer.
choices.why: This is a fact. Scientists can check it.

items.explain: "The best season" tells what someone thinks. Other people may like winter best, so it is an opinion.
items.hint: Which sentence cannot be proven?

items.prompt: Tap the sentence that is a fact.
items.say: Tap the sentence that is a fact.

choices.why: Creepiest tells what someone thinks. That is an opinion.
Should tells what someone thinks people ought to do. That is an opinion.

items.explain: You can count a spider's legs to prove it has eight. That makes it a fact. 🕷️
items.hint: Which sentence can be proven true?

items.prompt: What is the author's main purpose?
items.visual: Our town should build a bike path by the river. A bike path would give families a safe place to ride. Riding bikes is great exercise. More bikes would also mean fewer cars and cleaner air. Please tell the town council that you want a bike path!

choices.t: to persuade readers that the town should build a bike path
to explain how bikes are made
choices.why: The passage never tells how bikes are made.

choices.t: to tell a funny story about a bike ride
choices.why: There are no characters or story events. The author gives reasons.

items.explain: Clues: "Our town should build a bike path" and "Please tell the town council." The author wants to change your mind. 🚲
items.hint: Look for the words should and please.

items.prompt: What is the author's main purpose?
items.visual: Sloths live in the rainforests of Central and South America. They spend most of their lives hanging upside down in trees. Sloths move very slowly, which helps them save energy. Tiny green algae can grow in their fur. Sloths climb down to the ground only about once a week.

choices.t: to persuade readers to get a pet sloth
choices.why: The author never tells readers to do anything.

choices.t: to inform readers about how sloths live
to entertain readers with a made-up story
choices.why: The passage gives facts, not a story with characters.

items.explain: Every sentence gives a fact, like "Sloths move very slowly, which helps them save energy." The author wants to teach, or inform. 🦥
items.hint: Does the passage give facts, try to change your mind, or tell a story?

items.prompt: What is the author's main purpose?
items.visual: Pepper the parrot loved to copy sounds. When the phone rang, Pepper rang too. When Dad sneezed, Pepper sneezed even louder. One day, Pepper copied the doorbell so well that Mom ran to the door three times. Nobody was there, and Pepper laughed and laughed.

choices.t: to inform readers about how parrots talk
choices.why: The passage does not give facts about how parrots learn sounds.

choices.t: to persuade readers to buy a parrot
choices.why: The author never tries to change your mind.

choices.t: to entertain readers with a funny story

items.explain: Clue: "Pepper copied the doorbell so well that Mom ran to the door three times." It is a made-up, funny story, so the purpose is to entertain. 🦜
items.hint: Is this a real report or a silly story?

items.prompt: What is the author's point of view about homework?
items.visual: Some people think homework is a waste of time, but I think a little homework is helpful. It lets students practice what they learned in class. It also helps kids learn to plan their time. I believe ten minutes of reading each night is a great habit.

choices.t: Homework is a waste of time.
choices.why: The author says some people think this, but the author disagrees.

choices.t: A small amount of homework is helpful.
Students should do hours of homework every night.
choices.why: The author suggests ten minutes of reading, not hours.

items.explain: Clues: "I think a little homework is helpful" and "ten minutes of reading each night is a great habit." 📚
items.hint: Look for "I think" and "I believe."

items.prompt: Which sentence from the passage is an opinion?
items.say: Which sentence from the passage is an opinion?
items.visual: Yellowstone became the first national park in the United States in 1872. It has more than 500 geysers. Visitors can see bison, elk, and bears there. I think Yellowstone is the most exciting park in the country.

choices.t: Yellowstone became the first national park in the United States in 1872.
choices.why: This is a fact. You can check it in a history book.

choices.t: Visitors can see bison, elk, and bears there.
choices.why: This is a fact that can be proven.

choices.t: I think Yellowstone is the most exciting park in the country.

items.explain: "I think" and "most exciting" tell what the author believes. Other people may disagree, so it is an opinion.
items.hint: Opinion clue words: I think, best, most, should.

items.prompt: What does the author want readers to do?
items.visual: Birds need water, especially on hot summer days. A birdbath gives them a place to drink and clean their feathers. It is easy to make one with a shallow dish. Just change the water every few days. I hope you will set up a birdbath this week!

choices.why: The author wants to help birds, not catch them.
The author talks about wild birds outside, not pets.

items.explain: Clue: "I hope you will set up a birdbath this week!" That shows what the author wants. 🐦
items.hint: Read the last sentence.

items.prompt: Which sentence shows that polar bears are built for cold places?
items.visual: Polar bears live in the icy Arctic. A thick layer of fat under their skin keeps them warm. Polar bears can swim for hours. A newborn cub weighs only about one pound. Adult males can weigh more than 1,000 pounds.

choices.t: Polar bears can swim for hours.
choices.why: This is true, but it is about swimming, not about staying warm.

choices.t: A thick layer of fat under their skin keeps them warm.
A newborn cub weighs only about one pound.
choices.why: This is about size, not about the cold.

items.explain: The claim is about the cold. Only this sentence tells how polar bears stay warm. 🐻‍❄️
items.hint: Which sentence talks about staying warm?

items.prompt: Which sentence shows that ants are strong?
items.visual: Ants live in groups called colonies. Some ants can carry objects many times heavier than their own bodies. Ants talk to each other using smells. A colony may have thousands of ants. Ants have lived on Earth for millions of years.

choices.t: Some ants can carry objects many times heavier than their own bodies.
Ants talk to each other using smells.
choices.why: This is about how ants communicate, not how strong they are.

choices.t: Ants have lived on Earth for millions of years.
choices.why: This is about time, not strength.

items.explain: Carrying things many times heavier than yourself takes a lot of strength. That proves the claim. 🐜
items.hint: Which sentence tells what ants can lift?

items.prompt: Which sentence shows that Maya is curious?
items.visual: Maya found a strange shell on the beach. She turned it over and looked at every spiral. At home, she searched library books to find out what animal had lived inside. Maya also likes to play soccer.

choices.t: Maya found a strange shell on the beach.
choices.why: Finding a shell does not show that she wanted to learn about it.

choices.t: Maya also likes to play soccer.
choices.why: This is about Maya's hobby, not about being curious.

choices.t: At home, she searched library books to find out what animal had lived inside.

items.explain: Being curious means wanting to learn. Maya searched books to find out more. That proves it. 🐚
items.hint: Curious means wanting to find out more.

items.prompt: Which sentence shows that Death Valley can be very hot?
items.visual: Death Valley is a desert in California. It gets only about two inches of rain in a year. In summer, the temperature there can rise above 120 degrees Fahrenheit. Some tough plants and animals still live there.

choices.t: It gets only about two inches of rain in a year.
choices.why: This shows the desert is dry, not how hot it is.

choices.t: In summer, the temperature there can rise above 120 degrees Fahrenheit.
Some tough plants and animals still live there.
choices.why: This is about living things, not temperature.

items.explain: The claim is about heat. "Above 120 degrees" is the only sentence about temperature. 🌡️
items.hint: Which sentence gives a temperature?

items.prompt: Which sentence shows that dolphins are smart?
items.visual: Dolphins are mammals that live in the ocean. They breathe air through a blowhole on top of their heads. Scientists have seen dolphins use sea sponges to protect their noses while they search for food. Dolphins often swim in groups called pods.

choices.t: They breathe air through a blowhole on top of their heads.
choices.why: This is about breathing, not about being smart.

choices.t: Dolphins often swim in groups called pods.
choices.why: This is about how they travel, not about being smart.

choices.t: Scientists have seen dolphins use sea sponges to protect their noses while they search for food.

items.explain: Using an object as a tool takes smart thinking. That proves the claim. 🐬
items.hint: Which sentence shows a dolphin solving a problem?

items.prompt: Which sentence shows that Ethan is responsible?
items.visual: Ethan's class got a pet hamster named Nutmeg. Ethan asked to be her helper. Every morning, he gave Nutmeg fresh food and water without being reminded. Ethan thinks hamsters are cute.

choices.t: Every morning, he gave Nutmeg fresh food and water without being reminded.
Ethan's class got a pet hamster named Nutmeg.
choices.why: This tells about the class pet, not about Ethan.
Thinking a pet is cute does not show he takes care of it.

items.explain: Being responsible means doing your job without being told. Ethan fed Nutmeg every morning without being reminded. 🐹
items.hint: Responsible means doing your job every time.

items.prompt: Which sentence shows that recycling cans saves energy?
items.visual: Aluminum cans can be recycled again and again. Making a new can from a recycled can uses much less energy than making one from new metal. A recycled can may be back on a store shelf in about two months. Many cities pick up recycling each week.

choices.t: A recycled can may be back on a store shelf in about two months.
choices.why: This is about how fast it happens, not about energy.

choices.t: Making a new can from a recycled can uses much less energy than making one from new metal.
Many cities pick up recycling each week.
choices.why: This is about pickup, not about energy.

items.explain: The claim is about energy. Only this sentence says recycling uses much less energy. ♻️
items.hint: Which sentence uses the word energy?

items.prompt: Which sentence shows that young sunflowers follow the Sun?
items.visual: Sunflowers can grow taller than a grown-up. Young sunflower plants turn their heads to face the Sun as it moves across the sky. Their seeds are a favorite food for birds. Sunflowers grow best in warm, sunny places.

choices.t: Sunflowers grow best in warm, sunny places.
choices.why: This is true, but it shows sunflowers like sun, not that they move to follow it.

choices.t: Young sunflower plants turn their heads to face the Sun as it moves across the sky.
Their seeds are a favorite food for birds.
choices.why: This is about seeds, not about following the Sun.

items.explain: Following the Sun means turning as the Sun moves. Only this sentence says that. 🌻
items.hint: Which sentence tells about the plant moving?
